name: ALG12-CDG (CDG-Ig)
aliases: congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ig

reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: An N-linked type I CDG caused by biallelic ALG12 variants affecting a mannosyltransferase in endoplasmic reticulum assembly of the lipid-linked oligosaccharide
Presents in infancy with developmental delay, hypotonia, microcephaly, dysmorphic features and failure to thrive
Recurrent infections with hypogammaglobulinaemia are a notable feature, reflecting hypoglycosylation of immunoglobulins
Genital and skeletal abnormalities and feeding difficulties are also reported within the phenotype
Serum transferrin isoelectric focusing shows a type I pattern from under-occupancy of N-glycan sites
Coagulopathy and hepatic involvement can occur as part of the multisystem picture
Management is supportive and multidisciplinary; ALG12 sequencing confirms the diagnosis after a suggestive transferrin pattern
reference.pathophysiology: ALG12 encodes a dolichol-phosphate-mannose-dependent mannosyltransferase that adds a mannose residue during endoplasmic reticulum assembly of the dolichol-linked oligosaccharide precursor. Deficiency leaves an incomplete precursor that is transferred inefficiently or as a truncated glycan, causing under-occupancy of N-linked sites and a type I transferrin pattern. Hypoglycosylation of immunoglobulins and other proteins contributes to the recurrent infections, developmental and multisystem features. The defect lies in precursor assembly and transfer rather than glycan processing, consistent with its type I classification.
additionalDifferentials: Other type I CDG subtypes (e.g. PMM2-CDG, ALG1-CDG, ALG3-CDG)
Primary immunodeficiency with recurrent infection and hypogammaglobulinaemia
Syndromic causes of microcephaly with developmental delay
Chromosomal or copy-number syndromes with dysmorphism
additionalInvestigations: Transferrin isoelectric focusing or mass spectrometry demonstrating a type I pattern
Immunoglobulin levels and immune function assessment
Coagulation studies and liver function tests
Neuroimaging for microcephaly and structural change
redFlags: Recurrent or severe infections indicating clinically significant immunodeficiency
Failure to thrive with multi-organ involvement
reference.prognosis: ALG12-CDG causes lasting neurodevelopmental disability, and outcome depends heavily on the frequency and severity of infections and other systemic complications. Severity varies with residual enzyme function.
pitfalls: Investigating recurrent infection as isolated immunodeficiency without recognising an underlying CDG
Confusing the type I transferrin pattern with secondary causes
Assuming disease-modifying therapy exists when care is supportive
references: Scriver's OMMBID, congenital disorders of glycosylation
Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics, disorders of glycosylation
management: No disease-specific therapy exists; care is supportive and coordinated by a metabolic multidisciplinary team
Immunoglobulin replacement and prompt antimicrobial treatment of infections given hypogammaglobulinaemia
Anticonvulsant therapy and developmental support for seizures, hypotonia and delay
Nutritional support for failure to thrive with enteral feeding when required
Monitor and correct coagulopathy and manage associated hepatic involvement
Endocrine and growth surveillance with management of associated abnormalities
Genetic counselling and family testing for this autosomal recessive condition
